subject: Proposal: Renewal restructure & interim price hold for AstraHealth
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@astrahealth.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: AstraHealth renewal — capacity step-up + price hold ask

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the chat this morning. Per your team, AstraHealth is planning a staged migration of two high-throughput pipelines in Q3 which would push you ~40% over current commit for the second half of the year. I wanted to start the renewal/concession conversation so we can avoid any surprises come Oct.

Quick summary of the ask you shared: temporary 6-month price hold on current committed rate while capacity is stepped up by an additional 20% (phased), and a one-time credit to offset migration rework.

Proposed next steps from our side:
- I can pull together a sketch of a conditional amendment that includes a limited price hold, phased capacity add-on, and a credit schedule.
- If that looks reasonable, we put a formal 1-page amendment and route to procurement/legal.

Looping Tessa on approvals (she's on renewals sign-off) — Tessa, flagged for pricing flexibility + any guardrails you want to add.

Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: AstraHealth_Q1_usage_summary.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@astrahealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@astrahealth.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 13:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: AstraHealth renewal — capacity step-up + price hold ask

Ben —

Appreciate the quick follow-up. Correct on the ask. A few clarifications from procurement:
- The price hold needs to be visible in the amendment and not conditional on usage. We want a clear 6-month guaranteed rate.
- Credits should be structured: 50% upfront for migration runbook + 50% once both pipelines are live in prod.
- We also need a cap on monthly burst pricing while the step-up occurs — otherwise finance won't accept the exposure.

Can you send a redline or even a summary term sheet we can review with procurement. Prefer to keep this to a short amendment rather than a full MSA amendment.

Thanks,
Elena Ortiz
Head of Platform Partnerships | AstraHealth

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@astrahealth.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AstraHealth renewal — capacity step-up + price hold ask

Elena —

Thanks, that's helpful. I'm attaching a draft one-page amendment that mirrors your asks: flat 6-month price hold (June–Nov 2026), a phased +20% capacity addendum (50% immediate, 50% after 90 days), and a two-stage credit of $80k (40k upfront / 40k on go-live). I've also added a monthly burst cap during the 90-day phase to keep finance comfortable.

If that structure looks okay to you, Tessa can approve on our side to move this to legal. Marissa — can you confirm the credit accounting treatment and whether we can include a minor SLA carve (latency SLO) as part of the go-live definition?

Ben
Attachments: redwood-renewal-amendment-draft-v2.docx (DOCX, 25KB)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@astrahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AstraHealth renewal — capacity step-up + price hold ask

Elena / Ben —

Thanks for the draft and the clear asks. I reviewed the amendment and have the following adjustments before Tessa-side approval:

1) Price hold term: agree to a 6-month firm price hold, but tie it to the existing committed SKU set (no new SKU additions during the hold). This protects pricing integrity.
2) Capacity phase: the +20% will be capacity-credit based (non-billable until the final 90-day milestone completes), so we don't double-bill during the migration window.
3) Credit timing: OK to split 50/50 but we'd prefer the second credit to be payable 30 days after verified prod traffic (not on the calendar date) to allow ops validation.
4) Burst cap: we'll set a temporary burst ceiling of 2.5x current committed rate during the phase period. Any usage above that will be billed at a staged overage rate but eligible for a post-period true-up if there was an implementation failure attributable to Redwood.

If AstraHealth accepts these modifications, I will sign off the commercial terms and we can send to legal for a quick redline. Elena, can you confirm procurement is fine with the non-billable credit-crediting approach and the 30-day validation window for the second credit?

Tessa Morgan
Head of Renewals | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AstraHealth renewal — capacity step-up + price hold ask

Tessa / Ben —

Quick update following legal + finance review: both teams are comfortable with the proposed structure with small edits. Finance asked that the amendment include a one-line alloc code for the credit so we can route the $80k correctly (I'll add). Legal suggested tightening the go-live definition to include a short checklist (runbook executed, <10% error rate for 7 days, traffic validated) — that aligns to your validation window, Tessa.

I've updated the draft and attached the redline that we will send to AstraHealth pending their sign-off on the non-billable capacity-credit approach.

Next steps:
- Ben: send updated redline to Elena + procurement and ask for a 72-hour review window.
- Elena: confirm procurement accepts the allocation/code approach and the 30-day post-validation credit remit.
- If accepted, legal will prep final amendment for countersignature and we target execution by end of May.

Marissa Cole
Director, Renewals Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-renewal-amendment-draft-v2.docx (redline)
